clue.text: Snag people and roughly tear article in zone come from?

parts.note: to snag something is to catch it
men stands for people in general

indicators.note: roughly says the following word is handled loosely, its letters thrown into a new order

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instructions for snagging people and tearing at an article, with an odd question tagged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges TEAR to TARE. The definition is a playful description: the district a school's pupils or a hospital's patients come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchment area is the district served by a school or hospital, the place its users live.

clue.text: A record in the balance? Express regret

indicators.note: in says the word for record sits inside the word for balance

parts.note: poise means balance or equilibrium
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a disc is in the balance, then saying sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to say you are sorry, expressing regret.

clue.text: Giving credit to idiot is very stupid

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A remark that crediting a fool is itself foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass means grossly stupid or insensitive.

clue.text: Viewer's self-expression being one of disbelief?

explanation.surface: A viewer expressing themself with a look of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is an eye (a viewer) belonging to the speaker; as a whole it is an old exclamation meaning 'nonsense!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first reading is an eye that is the speaker's own; the second is an old exclamation voicing disbelief, like 'nonsense!'.

clue.text: Tentatively roused surly one about five

indicators.note: roused means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone timidly waking a grumpy person at around five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roused' stirs SURLY, ONE and V (five) together; 'about' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something tentatively means doing it hesitantly, with anxiety.

clue.text: A new tedious task, to import silver in Alaskan port

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the word for silver goes inside the chore

parts.note: a chore is a dull routine job
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A dull new job importing silver through a harbour in Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorage is the largest city in Alaska, a port on Cook Inlet.

clue.text: Concluding part of poem from some hidden voices

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The end of a poem spoken by unseen voices.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoi is a short closing stanza that ends certain poems, such as a ballade.

clue.text: Too many deliveries take steps to grab a cake

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so the dance and the deliveries clutch the other pieces between them

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
to dance is to step to music
a bun is a small cake

explanation.surface: A bowler's deliveries, a dance step and a cake grabbed along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' has the deliveries and the dancing clutch the cake. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, so 'deliveries' is not about the post.
explanation.definitionFit: An overabundance is an excess, more than is needed.

clue.text: It tests Roman power? Could be

definitions.text: It tests Roman power? Could be

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: could be says the preceding letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a religious movement challenges the authority of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges IT TESTS ROMAN, with P (power) in front. Read as a whole, the clue describes the Reformation challenge to the Pope's authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Protestantism arose as a challenge to the authority of the Roman Catholic Church and its Pope.

clue.text: Instrument the heartless abuse?

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A musician ill-treating an instrument without feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate is to abuse or desecrate something.

clue.text: Insure again, and do better

explanation.surface: Taking out a new policy and improving your lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two parts it means to put a fresh policy over something; as a whole word it means to get well or regain ground.

clue.text: They cover floors, eliminating line? Wrong

indicators.note: wrong means the remaining letters are put the wrong way, rearranged
eliminating means a letter is taken out of the word for floors

explanation.surface: Asking whether coverings over floors should drop a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking L out of FLOORS leaves FOORS, which 'Wrong' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofs sit over buildings, covering what is beneath.

clue.text: English colonel is got up elaborately — a green type

indicators.note: got up elaborately suggests dressed up fancily, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English army officer dressed up elaborately as an environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up elaborately' rearranges IS GOT to OGIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A green is an environmentalist, and an ecologist studies or campaigns for the natural environment.

clue.text: Pipe bringing air back into old railway system

indicators.note: into says the turned word goes inside the railway letters

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway

indicators.note: back means the word is written backwards

explanation.surface: A pipe bringing air back into an old railway network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AIR into RIA. BR stands for British Rail, the UK's nationalised railway until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A briar is a tobacco pipe carved from the root of a heath shrub.

clue.text: Arbiter going wrong, and passing on

parts.note: a referee is an arbiter, shortened to ref
erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: A referee making a mistake while passing the ball on.
explanation.definitionFit: Referring a matter is passing it on to someone else.

clue.text: Philosopher upset at screeds produced

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A thinker irritated by lengthy writings put before him.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was the French philosopher behind 'I think, therefore I am'.

clue.text: Assiduousness I cover over with information on church

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
gen is British slang for information
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A diligent person covering something with church information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns I LID into DILI. GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligence is careful, persistent effort, the same quality as being assiduous.

clue.text: Dog bit, in the end

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail or follow them
a piece is a bit

explanation.surface: A dog's bite, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb 'to follow'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a closing part or ending added to something.

clue.text: Wild fun -yelled in a wanting way?

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone yelling about fun out of desperate need.
explanation.definitionFit: Needfully means out of need, as from a lack or want.

clue.text: Flower girl in South Africa following priest

indicators.note: following puts the South African letters after the priest

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A girl selling flowers in South Africa, behind a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza Doolittle is the Cockney flower seller in Shaw's play Pygmalion.

clue.text: Change goes, perhaps, for second characters?

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: perhaps says goes is one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A change happens, maybe, to some secondary characters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self, another personality a person adopts.

clue.text: Volunteer soldiers with new energy in dance

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers getting fresh energy on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Fancy icons for a descendant

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate, so the letters are arranged decoratively anew

explanation.surface: Ornate religious images passed down to an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is an heir or a younger member of a family line.

clue.text: Move plant drunk brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the word is written in reverse

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk carrying a plant home.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot a plant is to shift it into a new container.

clue.text: Man to master alphabet to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man trying to master the alphabet, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a male first name, standing for any man.

clue.text: Send off for party symbol

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the political party
a sign is a symbol

explanation.surface: Sending off for a political party's emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to dispatch them to someone.

clue.text: Badly made sills round Newcastle region will lead to complaint

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the region letters
badly made says the letters of sills are put together wrongly

parts.note: NE is the north-east of England, where Newcastle is

explanation.surface: Shoddy window sills in the Newcastle area leading to complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly made' rearranges the sills, and 'round' wraps them about the north-east letters; 'will lead to' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, a medical sense of sickness.

clue.text: Joking language in impertinence

parts.note: a tongue is a language
cheek is impertinence

explanation.surface: Language used with impertinence in jest.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something with mock seriousness is speaking ironically, not meaning it.
